scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: My laptop (LAPTOP1, on the office WiFi) says it is
connected to the wireless -- full bars -- and yet nothing loads, I cannot
get anywhere at all. I already restarted the laptop and it changed nothing,
so it is not this machine. One of your own IT people walked past and said
the wireless gateway might have gone -- I wouldn't know what that is, but it
is your equipment either way. Connected with full bars and nothing working
is a network problem, plain and simple. Get the wireless actually working
again today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Campus DNS service (BIND/named) on srv1 (10.5.0.4). Laptop1 is receiving DNS settings that point to this server.

Mechanism: Laptop1 has working L2/L3 to the WiFi gateway and beyond (eth0 10.6.0.100/24, default via 10.6.0.1; ping to 10.6.0.1 OK; ping to 10.5.0.4 OK). However, name resolution fails: resolv.conf on Laptop1 contains “nameserver 10.5.0.4” and getent hosts example.com returns no result; curl to example.com returns HTTP code 000 (DNS failure). The DNS daemon on srv1 is listening on 10.5.0.4:53 (named), but is configured as non-recursive/authoritative-only. Its /etc/bind/named.conf.options explicitly sets “recursion no;” and only serves a local zone (“jeremysitlab.com”). Thus any external domain queries are refused, making “nothing load” for users.

Localization: srv1 process named (pid 29) bound to 10.5.0.4:53; WiFi gateway at dswa2 (10.6.0.1/32) is reachable and functioning. ARP on Laptop1 shows gateway MAC matching dswa2.

Root cause: DNS server misconfiguration on srv1 with recursion disabled, while clients are configured to use it for general internet name resolution.

Corrective fix: On srv1, enable recursion in /etc/bind/named.conf.options (recursion yes;) and configure forwarders to upstream resolvers (e.g., 1.1.1.1; 8.8.8.8;) or allow full recursion with root hints, then reload named (systemctl reload named). Alternatively, change DHCP/client configs to use a working recursive resolver. After this, clients (including WiFi) will resolve external sites normally.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly confirms LAPTOP1 is on 10.6.0.100, can ping its gateway 10.6.0.1, and ARP/gateway MAC shows dswa2 owning the virtual gateway IP, matching the healthy baseline.

The investigation captured relevant observations (client IP/config, connectivity to gateway and DNS server, inability of getent to resolve, named process present) but key assertions about server configuration (recursion=no, authoritative-only for external names) lack explicit evidence and the causal link to a misconfiguration is not fully demonstrated.
